edits.before: <term id="import-auto-id1426896">Temperature</term> is operationally defined to be what we measure with a thermometer. <emphasis effect="italics"/>(Many physical quantities are defined solely in terms of how they are measured. We shall see later how temperature is related to the kinetic energies of atoms and molecules, a more physical explanation.)
edits.after: <term id="import-auto-id1426896">Temperature</term> describes a system’s thermal state. Systems in thermal equilibrium have the same temperature. When systems at different temperatures can exchange energy as heat, the net transfer is from higher to lower temperature. A thermometer measures temperature by reaching thermal equilibrium with the system being measured.

edits.before: Again, temperature is the quantity measured by a thermometer.
It is an <emphasis effect="italics">absolute temperature</emphasis> scale defined to have 0 K at the lowest possible temperature, called <term id="import-auto-id1218210">absolute zero</term>.
edits.after: <term id="import-auto-id1218210">Absolute zero</term>, 0 K, is the lower limit of the Kelvin temperature scale.

edits.before: <meaning id="fs-id1806180">the quantity measured by a thermometer</meaning>
edits.after: <meaning id="fs-id1806180">a quantity describing thermal state; equal temperatures characterize thermal equilibrium, and temperature differences determine the direction of spontaneous heat transfer</meaning>
